series.name: Out of every RMB 100 of revenue, 2025

components.text: At one listed game company that sells a lot abroad, selling expenses ran more than 11 times R&D

components.title: From its annual report
components.text: selling expenses fell "mainly because internet traffic costs fell"

footnote: Source: 37 Interactive Entertainment, 2025 Annual Report. Shares of revenue and multiple calculated, selling expenses are group-wide
notes: Going abroad, the biggest bill is not development. It is traffic. Take the annual report of one listed game company with a large overseas business: in 2025, out of every RMB 100 of revenue, RMB 48.6 went to selling expenses and only RMB 4.3 to R&D, less than a ninth of it. Its own report says selling expenses fell mainly because internet traffic costs fell. To be fair about it: this is group-wide, not all overseas user acquisition, and it is one company. The ratio was 55.7% in 2024 and 51.7% in the first half of 2026. The direction is clear: user acquisition is the single biggest cost of going abroad.
